title: fuel oil malaysia prefchem refinery heads us first time since 2023 2026 08 14
text:
SINGAPORE, August 14 (Reuters) - A fuel oil cargo from Malaysia's PRefChem is heading to the United States for the first time since ​2023, shipping data showed, as disruptions from the Iran war ‌keep global availability of refinery feedstocks tight.
The low-sulphur and straight-run (LSSR) cargo can be fed into a refining unit to produce higher-margin distillates such as gasoline and diesel. ​The last fuel oil cargo from PRefChem to the U.S. ​shipped in May 2023, according to Kpler and LSEG data.
The ⁠Solomon Sea departed from the Vopak Dialog Pengerang terminal on August ​8 loaded with over 540,000 barrels of LSSR fuel and is scheduled ​to arrive in the United States in early September, Kpler data showed.
The cargo is heading to a refinery on the U.S. West Coast, a source familiar with the ​matter said.
State-owned Petronas, which owns the 300,000 barrel-per-day PRefChem refinery in ​Pengerang, did not respond to a request for comment.
Robust refining margins are supporting refinery ‌demand ⁠for feedstocks globally, while supplies remain tight due to the U.S.-Iran war.
Typically, U.S. refiners import fuel oil from nearer regions such as Mexico and Venezuela.
Meanwhile, PRefChem has sold more fuel oil for August loading via ​recent tenders, trade ​sources said, with ⁠three other cargoes of about 540,000 barrels each of the LSSR atmospheric residue scheduled to load in August.
One ​cargo loaded between August 12 and 13, ship-tracking ​data showed, ⁠while the other two were offered for loading between August 21 and 22 and August 30 and 31.
The refinery's atmospheric distillation unit was offline ⁠from June ​21 to July 10, according to data ​from energy consultancy IIR, which tracks refinery outages.
PRefChem typically produces gasoline and diesel, sporadically producing ​fuel oil.
